newsitem.title: LEBANON: ATHLETICS-LEBANON BARS IRAQ FROM PAN ARAB GAMES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-LEBANON BARS IRAQ FROM PAN ARAB GAMES.

text.p: Lebanon has excluded Iraqi athletes from the Pan Arab Games which open in Beirut on Saturday, sources close to the games said on Tuesday.
"The Iraqis don't have any visas to come to Lebanon. They will not get visas," said one of the sources.

"Because diplomatic ties between Lebanon and Iraq have been severed, we cannot welcome Iraq unless we receieve an order from the political authorities," Zeid Khyami, director-general of the sports ministry, which is in charge of organising the games, told Reuters.
"Until now we have not recieved such an order, so we cannot welcome the Iraqi athletes."
He said Lebanon decided to exclude Iraq from the games due to pressure from Kuwait and other Gulf Arab states.
Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman -- had threatened to boycott the Pan Arab Games if Iraq participated, a source said.
Pan Arab Games officials made the draw on Monday for three events -- football, basketball and volleyball. Iraq was not included.
Kuwait, still haunted by memories of the 1990 Iraqi invasion of their tiny oil-rich state, last month threatened to boycott any events in the games involving competitors from Iraq.
Kuwait says Iraq still holds some 600 Kuwaitis captured in the Gulf War, a charge denied by the Baghdad government.
Iraq and Kuwait were among 20 countries due to take part in the two-week games which Lebanon has been heavily promoting on television.

Lebanon, which has close ties with Kuwait, severed diplomatic ties with Baghdad in 1994 after the murder of an Iraqi dissident in Beirut. Four Iraqi diplomats suspected of involvement in the slaying were held in jail for three years. One of them died in jail.

Kuwait and Saudi Arabia have contributed substantially to the $50 million cost of building the 50,000-seat Beirut stadium at which many of the games' events will be held. They have also contributed millions of dollars to Lebanon's reconstruction.
The stadium was destroyed in an Israeli air raid during the Jewish state's 1982 invasion of Lebanon.
